title: Fast charging of quantum batteries assisted by nonlinear couplings
authors: Y. -J. Shen, Y. -C. Shen, C. -H. Chu, H. H. Jen
abstract: Charger-mediated quantum batteries offer promising opportunities for efficient energy transfer and storage at the quantum level, with potential advantages beyond their classical counterparts. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that nonlinear charger-battery interactions can substantially accelerate the charging of quantum batteries. In the weak-driving regime, sufficiently strong nonlinear coupling can dominate over the effect of dephasing and significantly reduce the charging time. In the strong- and optimal-driving regimes, where the optimal driving strength maximizes the steady-state ergotropy in the linear-coupling regime, nonlinear coupling gives rise to a new optimum in the charging time beyond that of the linear-coupling regime, accompanied by nearly critically damped dynamics. Remarkably, even in the absence of external driving, nonlinear coupling alone can substantially reduce the charging time, providing an alternative route toward fast battery charging. Our results establish nonlinear charger-battery coupling as an effective resource for accelerating quantum-battery charging and broaden the scope of interaction-enabled quantum advantages in energy transfer and storage.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates that nonlinear coupling between a charger and a quantum battery can substantially accelerate the rate of energy charging. By analyzing the system dynamics under various driving conditions, the authors show that nonlinear interactions provide a unique resource for enhancing energy storage efficiency. This finding broadens the understanding of interaction-enabled quantum advantages in energy transfer.
main_problem: The paper investigates how nonlinear couplings can accelerate the charging process of quantum batteries, aiming to find energy transfer mechanisms superior to classical or linear quantum models.
main_result: Nonlinear charger-battery interactions significantly accelerate charging time, establishing nonlinear coupling as an effective resource for energy storage, even surpassing the performance of external driving fields.
method: The study uses theoretical modeling based on the density matrix evolution governed by a master equation incorporating linear, nonlinear, and driving terms.
model_or_system: The system is a charger-mediated quantum battery, modeled by a Hamiltonian including linear ($g_1$) and nonlinear ($g_2$) coupling terms, and evolving under dissipation ($\gamma_C$) and external driving ($F$).
key_observables: Charging Time ($	au$), Battery Energy ($E_B$), and Ergotropy (quantifying extractable work).
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($g_1, g_2$), driving field strength ($F$), and dephasing rate ($\gamma_C$); analysis covers weak, strong, and optimal driving regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the resonance condition ($\omega_C = \omega_B = \omega_D$) and compares results across different coupling regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of energy and ergotropy, and plot charging time ($	au$) versus dephasing rate ($\gamma_C$) for various coupling strengths, demonstrating the reduction in $	au$ due to $g_2$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the system Hamiltonian and master equation, deriving key observables like energy and ergotropy, and then systematically analyzing the impact of nonlinear coupling ($g_2$) across different driving regimes (weak, strong, and undriven) to quantify the acceleration of charging dynamics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics, specifically energy transfer and non-equilibrium thermodynamics, which are central to AMO physics and quantum optics.
